thought.text: I found the root cause: the `tooling` Dockerfile copies `/usr/lib` from the node image (which has apk-tools 3.0.6) into the php image (which has apk-tools 3.0.8), causing a library mismatch that breaks the `apk` binary. I'll fix this by backing up and restoring the php image's libapk file.

reasoning_content:
Confirmed root cause:

- php:8.3-cli-alpine3.23 base image: `apk-tools-3.0.8-r0`, `/usr/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0` dated Sep 1
- node:20-alpine3.23: `apk-tools-3.0.6-r0`, `/usr/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0` dated Apr 14, 2026

The tooling Dockerfile does `COPY --from=node /usr/lib /usr/lib`, which clobbers `/usr/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0` with the older 3.0.6 libapk, but /sbin/apk remains the 3.0.8 binary that requires `apk_fs_is_malicious_filename` (a symbol added in 3.0.7+? or thereabouts). Hence the relocation error occurs.

Fix: after the COPY step in tooling.Dockerfile, restore apk-tools to the version present in the base image, or simply run `apk add --no-cache apk-tools` (which reinstalls 3.0.8). Since `apk add` needs a working apk... it doesn't — apk is broken! The apk binary is failing because of the library. Hmm, can we fix apk when apk itself is broken?

Options:
1. `apk add --force-broken apk-tools` — apk needs to work to install apk-tools. The apk binary is broken, so this won't work.
2. Manually download the apk-tools 3.0.8 .apk and extract libapk.so.3.0.0 into /usr/lib.
3. Reorder: copy node's /usr/lib before installing apk packages... the base image already has apk-tools, and the COPY clobbers it. Better: copy node's /usr/lib but preserve libapk. Or copy the node files in a way that skips libapk.

Simplest and most robust fix in the Dockerfile: after the COPY step, fetch the correct libapk from the alpine 3.23 repo:

```
RUN wget -q https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/v3.23/main/x86_64/apk-tools-3.0.8-r0.apk -O /tmp/apk-tools.apk && \
    busybox unzip -o /tmp/apk-tools.apk "lib/libapk.so.3.0.0" -d /tmp/apk-extract && \
    cp /tmp/apk-extract/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0 /usr/lib/ && ...
```

Hmm, but the exact version in the repo might have moved (3.0.8-r0 was the image at the time). Better to fetch the latest apk-tools for alpine 3.23 main. Actually, wait: the apk in the base php image is 3.0.8-r0 (Sep 1 build date — is that Alpine 3.23's stable?). Actually, let me check what apk-tools versions are available for alpine 3.23. But careful: if I install a newer apk-tools (e.g., 3.0.10) whose binary expects a different libapk — the .apk contains both the /sbin/apk binary and lib, so extracting the whole apk fixes both consistently.

Even simpler: extract all files from the latest apk-tools-*.apk into the root filesystem:

```
RUN ARCH=$(uname -m) && \
    wget -qO /tmp/apk.apk https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/v3.23/main/$ARCH/apk-tools-<ver>-r0.apk && \
    (cd /tmp && busybox unzip -o apk.apk 'sbin/apk' 'lib/libapk.so.3.0.0' ... )
```

But what's the current version? I can query the APKINDEX. Let me check what version is currently available for alpine 3.23 main x86_64.

Alternative, cleaner approach: fix the Dockerfile so the node COPY doesn't clobber apk-tools. E.g., change the copy order: do the COPY from node first, then `apk add --force-reinstall apk-tools`? No wait — the base php image's apk is working (3.0.8), so at that point `apk add` works. If I do the COPY after all the apk add steps... actually, in the current Dockerfile, the `apk update && apk add ...` step happens after the COPY. The apk that runs during `apk add` is the broken one (3.0.8 binary + 3.0.6 lib). Hmm, wait, no — look at the build log: the build got through step 12 `RUN apk update && apk add ...` and step 13 (docker-php-ext-configure) failed. So apk add worked?? Interesting — `docker-php-ext-configure` invokes php-configure, which may call apk... the error appears at the point where docker-php-ext-configure runs (exit code 127 with an apk relocation error). So apk actually worked during apk update/add (maybe because at that point the apk binary is 3.0.8 + lib 3.0.6... no wait, the relocation error means the apk binary is trying to use symbols not in lib 3.0.6. If it's broken, how did apk update work?

Hmm, wait. Let me re-read. Step 12: `RUN apk update && apk add ...` — this completed (log shows step 13 failing). So apk worked fine there. Then step 13 `docker-php-ext-configure gd` failed with apk relocation error. Strange. Maybe... `docker-php-ext-configure` doesn't call apk. Let me look at what docker-php-ext-configure does: it runs `phpize` and `php-config` and configure... maybe it calls `apk` via...? Hmm, exit code 127 means "command not found" — the /sbin/apk binary failed to load (dynamic linker relocation error → shell reports 127). So something in docker-php-ext-configure's path is invoking apk. Actually, does `docker-php-ext-configure` source /usr/local/bin/docker-php-ext-configure, which calls `apk add --virtual .build-deps` if not yet done? Let me recall the php docker image scripts:

```
docker-php-ext-configure() {
    ...
    # if this is the first time, install build deps
    if [ ! -d "$PHP_CPP_BUILD_DIR" ]; then ... apk add --virtual ... build deps
```

Yes! docker-php-ext-configure installs PHP's build dependencies via apk on the first run (gcc, make, etc.). The tooling image had already installed g++/make via a manual apk add step, but the image's "build deps" virtual package hasn't been installed, so docker-php-ext-configure tries `apk add --no-cache --virtual .php-build-deps ...`.

But then, why did step 12's apk add work? If libapk had been clobbered at the COPY point... hmm, wait, maybe I misread the order. Let me re-check the Dockerfile:

```
COPY --from=node /usr/lib /usr/lib      <- clobbers libapk
COPY --from=node /usr/local/share /usr/local/share
COPY --from=node /usr/local/lib /usr/local/lib
COPY --from=node /usr/local/include /usr/local/include
COPY --from=node /usr/local/bin /usr/local/bin

# Install Composer manually
COPY --from=composer/composer:latest-bin /composer /usr/bin/composer

# Show some usefull versions
RUN php -v && composer --version && node --version && npm --version && ...   <- step ~11/12?

# Configure GD (Required for media processing)
RUN docker-php-ext-configure gd ...  <- step 13
```

Wait, where's the `apk update && apk add` step? Let me recount the tooling Dockerfile:

1. FROM php:8.3-cli-alpine3.23 (stage-1 1/16)
2. ARG USER_ID... (ENV lines don't create steps)
3. RUN addgroup (2/16)
4. RUN adduser (3/16)
5. RUN chown (4/16)
6. RUN apk update && apk add ... (5/16)
7. COPY --from=node /usr/lib /usr/lib (6/16)
8. COPY /usr/local/share (7/16)
9. COPY /usr/local/lib (8/16)
10. COPY /usr/local/include (9/16)
11. COPY /usr/local/bin (10/16)
12. COPY composer (11/16)
13. RUN php -v && composer --version ... (12/16)
14. RUN docker-php-ext-configure gd (13/16) ← failed
15. RUN docker-php-ext-install gd zip pdo_mysql bcmath exif (14/16)
16. RUN docker-php-ext-configure intl && docker-php-ext-install intl (15/16)
17. RUN pecl install imagick ... (16/16)

So apk add in step 6 ran before the COPY clobbered libapk. That's why it worked. And step 13's docker-php-ext-configure called apk → boom.

So the fix: in the tooling Dockerfile, after the COPY from node, reinstall the correct apk-tools (either extract it from the alpine repo or use a different approach).

Best approach: modify the COPY to preserve libapk, or add a repair step. The cleanest minimal fix:

Option A: In tooling.Dockerfile, after the 5 COPY steps, add:
```
RUN apk add --force-reinstall --no-cache apk-tools
```
But wait — apk is broken at this point, so `apk add` won't run. Dead end.

Option B: Extract the apk-tools apk from the CDN. But which version matches? The php image has 3.0.8-r0. I can pin the download to exactly `apk-tools-3.0.8-r0.apk` from https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/v3.23/main/x86_64/. If the version has moved to r1, the file might no longer exist (alpine keeps the old version for a while, but it could be deleted from main). Safer: fetch the APKINDEX and parse the current version. That's more complex in a Dockerfile.

Option C: Reorder — move the node COPY to before `apk update && apk add ...`. Then the final apk add step would reinstall apk-tools? No — apk add doesn't reinstall packages that are already installed at the same version. The COPY clobbered libapk.so.3.0.0, but the apk-tools package is still "installed" per /lib/apk/db/installed, so `apk add` won't touch it. However, `apk fix` or `apk add --force-reinstall apk-tools` would work at that point (apk is still broken... no wait, if we copy first, apk is still broken by the time apk add runs. Same problem.

Hmm wait, no. If we do the COPY first, the apk binary is still 3.0.8 (from php base) and the lib is 3.0.6 (from node) → apk is broken from the start. Even worse.

Option D: Copy node's /usr/lib but exclude the apk-related files. COPY can't easily exclude. Alternative: after the COPY, restore libapk from a saved copy:

```
RUN cp /usr/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0 /tmp/libapk.so.bak   # must be done BEFORE the node COPY
COPY --from=node /usr/lib /usr/lib
RUN cp /tmp/libapk.so.bak /usr/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0
```

This is clean and deterministic: back up the base image's libapk before clobbering, restore it after. The apk-tools package metadata stays at 3.0.8, and the restored library matches the 3.0.8 binary.

But wait — the php base image's `apk add` in step 6 installed new packages (bash, imagemagick, etc.). Those might have pulled in a newer libapk? No, the apk add of those packages doesn't upgrade apk-tools unless it's a dependency. The php image is built with apk-tools 3.0.8. As long as the package installation doesn't trigger an apk-tools upgrade, the backup of libapk.so.3.0.0 (after apk add in step 6, before the COPY) is the safest point.

Actually, the simplest and most robust: do the backup+restore in a single RUN around the COPY? You can't sandwich a COPY between two RUNs in one RUN. But:

```
RUN cp /usr/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0 /lib/apk/
COPY --from=node /usr/lib /usr/lib
...
RUN cp /lib/apk/libapk.so.3.0.0 /usr/lib/
```

Wait, is libapk.so.3.0.0 the only relevant file? The libapk package installs /usr/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0, /usr/lib/libapk.so.3 (symlink?), and probably /usr/lib/libapk.a, /usr/include/apk*. Let me check what files apk-tools provides: /sbin/apk, /usr/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0, /usr/lib/libapk.so.3 (symlink), /usr/include/apk/*.h, /usr/lib/libapk.a, /usr/lib/pkgconfig/apk.pc.

The node COPY also copies /usr/local/bin, which includes node's npm etc. Fine.

To be safe, I can restore everything under /usr/lib/libapk* from a backup directory:

```
RUN mkdir -p /tmp/apkbackup && cp -a /usr/lib/libapk* /tmp/apkbackup/ 2>/dev/null || true
COPY --from=node /usr/lib /usr/lib
RUN cp -a /tmp/apkbackup/. /usr/lib/ && rm -rf /tmp/apkbackup
```

Hmm, wait, is there anything else in /usr/lib that node's COPY clobbers that apk needs? apk is a static binary? No — apk is dynamically linked against libapk.so.3.0.0. Just restoring libapk* should suffice.

Let me verify: does node's /usr/lib have other apk-related stuff? No.

Also, do the api Dockerfile (php:8.3-fpm-alpine3.23) or web Dockerfile have the same problem? The api Dockerfile doesn't COPY from node — it does direct apk adds and pecl installs. Its `docker-php-ext-install pdo_mysql` doesn't need to install build deps (pdo_mysql has no C extension deps? Actually, docker-php-ext-install compiles pdo_mysql but needs build deps; the api Dockerfile installs g++, make, autoconf... via apk add, and docker-php-ext-install only auto-installs build deps if phpize is needed... it might still call apk for virtual build deps). But the api image's apk isn't clobbered (no COPY from node), so it's fine.

The web Dockerfile is pure node:20-alpine — its apk is consistently 3.0.6. npm ci works.

So only the tooling Dockerfile needs fixing.

Plan:
1. Fix docker/tooling/tooling.Dockerfile: back up libapk before the node /usr/lib COPY, restore it after.
2. Re-run docker compose up -d --build.

Also, let me double-check whether `apk update` inside the tooling step (step 6) upgraded apk-tools to a version newer than the image's 3.0.8... apk update only updates the index, doesn't install. So after step 6, libapk is still the image's 3.0.8. Backup after step 6 (i.e., between steps 6 and 7) is exactly what my Dockerfile edit does (a RUN between them).

Wait, one more consideration: does the node image's /usr/lib contain a different libapk with the same SONAME? Yes, node's 3.0.6 lib is libapk.so.3.0.0. COPY overwrites it. Restore puts it back.

But also: does node's /usr/lib contain `libstdc++.so.6` etc., and could those be clobbered in a way that breaks PHP? The php base also has a libstdc++ (from the php image's apk? php:8.3-cli-alpine includes libstdc++). The node COPY might overwrite libstdc++ with the node version. Both are alpine 3.23, so versions are likely identical. The build was probably working before (this is the project's own Dockerfile, and it should have worked in CI at the time of the commit). The breakage is because alpine 3.23 was released/rebuilt after the commit: the php image's apk-tools was updated to 3.0.8 (Sep 1, 2026), while the node image stayed at 3.0.6 (Apr 14, 2026). Wait, that's odd — the node image's libapk is dated Apr 14, 2026, and php's is Sep 1, 2026. Both alpine3.23. Hmm, node:20-alpine3.23 was last rebuilt around April 2026, and php:8.3-cli-alpine3.23 was rebuilt in September 2026. Since then, apk-tools has been updated to 3.0.8 in alpine's main repo, and the `apk update && apk add` in the php base... no wait, the apk-tools version comes from the image build, not from our apk add.

Whatever the exact history, the evidence is clear: 3.0.8 binary + 3.0.6 library = broken. My fix (restore the matching library) is correct.

Actually, an even cleaner alternative fix: after the COPY step, run `apk add --no-cache --force-reinstall apk-tools` — but apk is broken. Or install apk-tools from a tarball. My backup/restore approach avoids the network dependency.

Let me also consider: the api Dockerfile also uses php:8.3-fpm-alpine3.23. Its apk is 3.0.8, consistent within the image. No problem.

Alright, let me implement the fix.

action.command:
cd /workspace && cp docker/tooling/tooling.Dockerfile /tmp/tooling.Dockerfile.bak && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
p = 'docker/tooling/tooling.Dockerfile'
s = open(p).read()
old = """# Copy files from node image
COPY --from=node /usr/lib /usr/lib"""
new = """# Back up the base image's libapk (the node image below ships an older
# libapk with the same SONAME and would break the apk binary when copied over)
RUN cp /usr/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0 /usr/local/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0.base

# Copy files from node image
COPY --from=node /usr/lib /usr/lib
# Restore the base image's libapk so apk keeps working
RUN cp /usr/local/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0.base /usr/lib/libapk.so.3.0.0"""
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, new)
open(p, 'w').write(s)
print("patched")
EOF
grep -n -A3 -B1 'libapk' docker/tooling/tooling.Dockerfile
